key_insight: Recurrent neural networks trained for free recall do not just learn one standard memory rule—they discover multiple, human-like strategies for retrieving memories. The best-performing models use an index-based approach, similar to a "memory palace," rather than relying only on classical temporal context.
problem_solved: This paper addresses how to model free recall more realistically: can AI systems learn the diverse strategies humans use to remember items, instead of being limited to a single temporal-context explanation?
method: Train recurrent neural networks on free-recall tasks and optimize them to perform memory retrieval.
Compare learned model behavior against classical temporal context models and human recall patterns.
Analyze the top-performing networks to identify the internal retrieval strategy they use, including index-based mechanisms.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests that memory systems can benefit from richer, strategy-like retrieval mechanisms rather than a single fixed rule. It also provides a path for building more human-like memory models and better understanding how neural networks organize recall.

paper_title: A neural network model of free recall learns multiple memory strategies
paper_authors: Moufan Li, Kristopher T. Jensen, Qiong Zhang, Qihong Lu, Marcelo G. Mattar
